methodologyNotes: Roster covers fourteen handheld air plasma cutters spanning entry-level 20A hobbyist drag-torch units to 60A dual-voltage inverters and industrial 40-45A pilot-arc machines, verified 2026-08-11 primarily against manufacturer/brand product pages (Hypertherm, PrimeWeld, Lotos, YesWelder, Forney, Everlast, Weldpro) and authorized-dealer listings that mirror manufacturer spec sheets (Cyberweld for Hobart/Miller/ESAB-Thermal Dynamics, General Air and weldingsuppliesfromioc.com for Lincoln/Hypertherm, Farm & Fleet for Forney). Four adversarial corrections were made to the seed list, each documented in the affected product's provenance field: (1) "YesWelder CUT-55DS" is superseded in YesWelder's current catalog by the "CUT-55DS PLUS" (HF pilot-arc version) — corrected to the current SKU. (2) "Everlast PowerPlasma 62Si" does not exist in Everlast's catalog, past or present; the actual current 60A digital-inverter model is the PowerPlasma 62i (i-Series) — corrected accordingly. (3) "Herocut CUT45" is not an exact catalog name; HeroCut (an Amazon-marketplace budget brand) sells CUT35i, CUT45i, CUT45X and CUT45D as distinct listings — corrected to the CUT45X, the dual-voltage, pilot-arc-equipped listing matching the seed's implied spec class, with several fields left null where the Amazon listing content could not be fully retrieved. (4) "Weldpro Cut45" does not exist; Weldpro's current lineup is CUT40HF/CUT40NH/CUT60HF/CUT60NH — corrected to the CUT40NH ("Contact Pilot Arc", non-HF start), the nearest real 40A-class model, again with several fields left null rather than guessed. Two additional notes: the Hypertherm Powermax45 XP was discontinued by Hypertherm in March 2024 and replaced by the Powermax45 SYNC, but is retained here (as instructed by the seed list) using its last-documented dealer spec/price before discontinuation, flagged in its provenance; and the Lincoln Tomahawk 375 AIR is a compact 10-25A single-phase unit with a built-in air compressor (comparable to the Hypertherm Powermax30 AIR class), not a heavy 3-phase industrial machine as its "375" model branding might suggest to a reader unfamiliar with the line — also flagged, and it too shows as discontinued on lincolnelectric.com, sold through remaining distributor stock. Wherever a manufacturer or dealer page did not state a figure (severance thickness, duty cycle, air CFM, weight, or price), that field was left null rather than estimated by analogy to similar machines — this applies most heavily to the two corrected budget-brand entries (HeroCut CUT45X, Weldpro CUT40NH) whose marketplace listings could not be fully re-fetched at research time. accessedAt 2026-08-11 throughout.

products.name: Hypertherm Powermax45 XP Plasma Cutter
products.priceNote: Discontinued by Hypertherm in March 2024, replaced by the Powermax45 SYNC. Last documented dealer price for the 20 ft hand-torch package (SKU 088012) was $2,435.00 (weldingsuppliesfromioc.com, listed sold out at time of check).

specs.air_requirement: 400 scfh (6.7 CFM) @ 90 psi, clean/dry shop air

products.provenance: Retained from the seed list per instructions despite being discontinued. Dealer page (weldingsuppliesfromioc.com) explicitly states "This machine has been replaced by the Powermax 45 Sync (088560)" and lists it sold out at $2,435.00 for the 20 ft hand-torch package, so priceUsd is left null with the last-known figure recorded in priceNote rather than presented as a current, purchasable price. Cut thickness (5/8 in recommended, 1-1/8 in severance), duty cycle (50% @ 45A, 100% @ 32A), 200-240V 1-PH input, 400 scfh @ 90 psi air spec, and 31 lb (with torch) weight all confirmed on the same dealer page, which reproduces Hypertherm's factory spec sheet.

products.name: Hypertherm Powermax30 AIR Plasma Cutter (Built-In Compressor)
products.priceNote: Current retail price for the 'Building America' special-edition 15 ft torch package (SKU 088096) at weldingsuppliesfromioc.com; page lists a regular price of $2,615.00. Standard (non-special-edition) packages may be priced somewhat differently at other authorized dealers.

specs.air_requirement: Built-in compressor — no external air supply required

products.provenance: Dealer page confirms 120-240V 1-PH input, 15-30A output current, 35%/20% duty cycle, 29.8 lb weight with torch, and the defining feature of this model: an internal air compressor that eliminates the need for an external compressor/filter. No source fetched during research stated a distinct severance-cut figure (only the 5/16 in recommended-cut spec is consistently published), so sever_cut_thickness is left null rather than estimated.

products.name: PrimeWeld CUT60 Dual Voltage 60-Amp Plasma Cutter
products.priceNote: Current sale price on primeweld.com; page lists a regular price of $799.00.

specs.air_requirement: 5 CFM min @ 90 psi; 40-75 psi operating range

products.provenance: PrimeWeld's own product page confirms 20-60A output current, non-touch/blowback (non-HF, CNC-compatible) pilot arc, dual-voltage 120V/240V input, 30 lb weight, and cut capacity up to 7/8 in steel; the page's marketing copy separates a 1/2 in "quality/recommended" cut from the 7/8 in maximum, consistent with PrimeWeld's own published cut charts. Duty cycle and air pressure/flow figures taken directly from the same page.

products.name: Lotos LTP5000D 50A Non-Touch Pilot Arc Plasma Cutter
products.priceNote: MSRP $399.00 on lotosplasmacutter.com/Amazon; frequently discounted to roughly $300-350 across retailers.
products.provenance: Lotos's official product page confirms non-touch pilot-arc start, 10-50A output, 5/8 in clean-cut capacity, dual-voltage 110V/220V (auto-sensing) input, and 60% duty cycle at 50A on either voltage. Weight (20 lb) and air requirement (3.6 CFM @ 65 psi) corroborated on weldguru.com's review of the same model; severance thickness (3/4 in / 19mm) confirmed on the same review. A secondary Lotos-hosted page (uwelding.com) listed slightly different figures under the product name 'LTP5505D,' which appears to be a distinct/renamed SKU rather than the LTP5000D, so those figures were not used.

products.name: Lotos LT5000D 50A Air Plasma Cutter (Touch-Start)
products.priceNote: Exact current dealer price not confirmed via a direct manufacturer or retailer fetch at research time; historically priced roughly $100-130 below its pilot-arc sibling, the LTP5000D (~$399 MSRP).
products.provenance: The LT5000D is the touch/contact-start sibling of the LTP5000D (same 50A, dual-voltage 110V/220V platform, but the torch must physically touch the workpiece to strike an arc rather than using a non-touch pilot arc) — confirmed via comparison coverage (versusguy.com) and the model's own review coverage. Cut capacity (1/2 in mild steel clean cut), 21 lb weight (29 lb boxed), and 60% @ 50A duty cycle corroborated across search-indexed retailer/review copy. Air CFM/PSI requirement was not confirmed on any source successfully fetched, so it is left null rather than assumed identical to the LTP5000D.

products.name: Hobart AirForce 40i Plasma Cutter
products.priceNote: Current Cyberweld price for the 12 ft XT40R torch package (SKU 500576); page lists mfg price $2,573.00.
products.provenance: Cyberweld's listing (an authorized Hobart/Miller-family dealer reproducing the factory spec sheet) confirms 5/8 in clean cut at 60% duty cycle, 7/8 in maximum cut, 120V/240V MVP toolless-adapter input, a pilot-arc controller for expanded-metal/painted-surface cutting without retriggering, 6.0 CFM @ 90-120 psi air requirement, and 22 lb weight for the 12 ft torch package.

products.name: Miller Spectrum 625 X-TREME Plasma Cutter
products.priceNote: Current Cyberweld price for the 12 ft XT40 quick-connect torch package (SKU 907579); page lists mfg industrial price $3,179.57.
products.provenance: Cyberweld's official Miller dealer listing confirms 40A rated output (auto-reduced to 27A on 120V input via Auto-Line technology, 187-264V accepted), 5/8 in mild steel cutting capacity, non-HF pilot-arc starting, and 21 lb weight with the 12 ft torch. Severance cut thickness, duty cycle percentage, and air CFM/PSI requirement were not stated on the fetched page or corroborating search results, so those fields are left null rather than assumed from similarly-classed machines.

products.name: ESAB (Thermal Dynamics) Cutmaster 40 Plasma Cutter
products.priceNote: Current Cyberweld price for the 16 ft SL60 torch package (SKU 1-4000-1); page lists mfg price $3,014.86.
products.provenance: Sold under ESAB's legacy Thermal Dynamics brand name (ESAB now owns Thermal Dynamics); Cyberweld's dealer page confirms 1/2 in recommended pierce/cut capacity, 1 in maximum severance, 15-40A continuously adjustable output (27A @ 110V / 40A @ 200-240V auto-sensed), 22 lb weight, and the 16 ft SL60 1Torch with pilot-arc-capable Black Series electrode. Duty cycle breakdown (40%/60%/100%) and air flow/pressure spec corroborated via search-indexed retailer copy for the same SKU.

products.name: Forney Easy Weld 251 (20 P) Plasma Cutter
products.priceNote: Current Blain's Farm & Fleet retail price.
products.provenance: Farm & Fleet's listing (reproducing Forney's own spec copy) confirms 20A rated output on standard 120V household power, 1/4 in mild-steel/stainless and 3/16 in aluminum cut capacity, 35% duty cycle @ 20A, 1.5 CFM compressed-air requirement, and 21.5 lb weight. This is Forney's entry-level drag-torch unit — it uses 'Drag Torch Technology' (contact/touch starting) rather than a pilot arc, and Forney does not publish a separate severance-cut figure for this model, so pilot_arc is false and sever_cut_thickness is null.

products.name: YesWelder CUT-55DS PLUS Pilot Arc Plasma Cutter
products.priceNote: Current yeswelder.com price for the cutter only; bundle options with extra consumables/torch run $324.30-$360.30.
products.provenance: CORRECTED FROM SEED: the seed name 'CUT-55DS' is superseded in YesWelder's current catalog by the 'CUT-55DS PLUS' (HF pilot-arc start, listed on yeswelder.com under the same 55A dual-voltage product line, alongside a separate non-HF 'CUT-55NHF PLUS' variant); corrected to the currently sold PLUS SKU. YesWelder's own product page confirms 20-55A output (30A cap on 120V), dual-voltage 110V/220V ±10% input, HF pilot-arc starting, 14.48 lb weight, and the full clean/severance cut and duty-cycle tables at both voltages.

products.name: Lincoln Electric Tomahawk 375 AIR Plasma Cutter
products.priceNote: Current General Air Service & Supply price for the 10 ft torch package (SKU K2806-1). Lincoln Electric's own site (lincolnelectric.com/en/Products/k2806-1) marks the model DISCONTINUED; sold through remaining distributor/dealer stock.

specs.air_requirement: Built-in compressor — no external air supply required

products.provenance: Despite the '375' branding suggesting a larger industrial 3-phase machine, the Tomahawk 375 AIR is actually a compact single-phase (208-230V) unit with an internal air compressor, output continuously adjustable from 10-25A (rated 25A @ 90V) — confirmed via Lincoln's own product-title copy and the General Air dealer page, which both describe 'Continuous Output Control' and an 'Internal air compressor.' Recommended (5/16 in) and severance (1/2 in) cut thicknesses confirmed via Lincoln's product copy; a secondary '3/8 in max' figure also appears in some listings but was not used to avoid double-reporting a maximum alongside the severance rating. Duty cycle, pilot-arc status, and weight were not stated on any source successfully fetched (the manufacturer spec-sheet PDF link could not be retrieved), so those fields are left null rather than assumed. Lincoln's own product page confirms the model is discontinued.

products.name: Everlast PowerPlasma 62i IGBT Inverter Plasma Cutter
products.priceNote: Current sale price on everlastgenerators.com; page lists regular price $1,199.00.

specs.air_requirement: 6 CFM @ 90 psi (min. 30-gal tank); 75 psi recommended operating pressure

products.provenance: CORRECTED FROM SEED: no model named 'PowerPlasma 62Si' exists in Everlast's catalog, past or present. The seed appears to be a misremembering of the PowerPlasma 62i (i-Series), Everlast's actual current 60A digital-inverter plasma cutter (also sold with an optional CNC/mechanized torch package) — corrected accordingly. Everlast's own product page confirms 20-60A output, 220/240V 1-PH input, pilot-arc start, 3/4 in daily clean-cut and 1-1/4 in severance capacity, 60%/100% duty-cycle figures, 6 CFM @ 90 psi minimum air requirement (with 75 psi recommended operating pressure), and 53 lb weight.

products.name: HeroCut CUT45X Dual Voltage Plasma Cutter
products.priceNote: Amazon marketplace price for this listing fluctuates and was not reliably confirmed at research time; direct product-page fetch failed (server error).
products.provenance: CORRECTED FROM SEED: 'Herocut CUT45' is not an exact catalog name — HeroCut (an Amazon-marketplace budget brand) sells CUT35i, CUT45i, CUT45X, and CUT45D as distinct listings with different voltage/torch configurations. Corrected to the CUT45X, the dual-voltage (120V/240V) non-HF blowback pilot-arc listing whose title matches the seed's implied 45A dual-voltage spec class, per the listing title text: 'HeroCut 45X 120/240V Dual Voltage IGBT CNC Plasma Cutter Non-HF Pilot Arc Blowback Arc Starting ... 14mm Clean Cut.' A direct re-fetch of the Amazon listing returned a server error at research time, so severance cut, duty cycle, and weight — not independently corroborated elsewhere — are left null rather than guessed.

products.name: Weldpro CUT40NH Contact Pilot Arc Plasma Cutter
products.provenance: CORRECTED FROM SEED: no 'Weldpro Cut45' model exists — Weldpro's current lineup, confirmed on weldpro.com, is CUT40HF ($649.99), CUT40NH ($649.99), CUT60HF ($799.99), and CUT60NH ($799.99); there is no 45A model. Corrected to the CUT40NH, the nearest real current model (a 40A-class unit), whose Amazon listing title identifies it as a 'Contact Pilot Arc Plasma Cutter with Dual Voltage 220V/110V,' i.e. a non-HF, contact/blowback pilot-arc start. Output current range (15-40A @ 220V, 15-30A @ 110V) corroborated via search-indexed retailer copy for the same SKU. Cut thickness, duty cycle, and air requirement were not confirmed on any source successfully fetched at research time — the weldpro.com product subpage returned a 404 on direct re-fetch — so those fields are left null rather than guessed.
